#en: I keep replaying the last jump in my head, like staring at a cracked grav plate and waiting for it to give. On paper it was simple: log the new corridor data, tag the anomaly signatures, pass everything along to the next set of hands. Trade Authority gets leaner lanes, we get a bonus that does not show on any official docket. But the vectors we pulled do not line up with any sanctioned chart I have ever seen, and the noise in the telemetry felt wrong, like something out there breathing against the hull. I brought it up in passing back in Neon, over cheap coffee and louder music than the bar could handle, and the broker who gave us the coordinates just smiled, said some ex-Navy genius had triple-checked the math. Since then, every rumor I have heard about vanished haulers or convoys that never reached HopeTown seems to trace back to the same kind of shortcut. I have logged everything I can on this recorder and flagged a follow-up survey for whoever takes Windcrier after us, told them to trace the signal all the way to that old listening post sitting off the lanes like a forgotten ear. Someone will need to go there, see how deep this pattern really runs. If they are smart, they will not come alone.
zh: 我脑子里一直在重放最后那次跃迁，像盯着一块开裂的重力板等它崩掉。纸面上很简单：记录新的走廊数据、给异常特征打标、把一切转交给下一批人手。贸易管理局得到更精简的航道，我们得到一笔不出现在任何官方底账上的奖金。可我们提取的那些矢量，跟我见过的任何获批星图都对不上；而遥测里的噪声也不太对，像外面有什么东西贴着船壳呼吸。我在霓虹城随口提起这事，就着廉价咖啡和那间酒吧勉强招架得住的更响的音乐，给我们坐标的经纪商只是笑笑，说某个前海军天才把算式核对过三遍。从那以后，我听说的每一起关于失踪货船、或从未抵达希望镇的运输队的传言，似乎都能追溯到同一类捷径。我用这台录音机把能记的都记了下来，并为继我们之后接手风哭号的人标出一次后续勘测，叫他们把信号一路追到那座像一只被遗忘的耳朵一样悬在航道外的旧监听站。总得有人去那儿，看看这图案到底扎得多深。要是他们聪明，就不会一个人去。

#en:
I am logging this from a maintenance alcove on the relay because the walls here feel thicker, like they will actually keep a secret for once.

Spent the last six hours peeling back Trade Authority manifests with my own hands. The broker who used to sit this post thought he was clever, hiding patterns inside mislabels and "transmission errors." He was not clever enough. Buried in the duplicates and ghost shipments, there is a cluster of traffic tags that never resolve to any port, just loop back through the same defunct military uplink on the edge of nowhere. UC registry says that listening post went dark years ago, but the timestamps on these routings are fresh.

Everyone in the bar stories talks about a pilot who can find ships after they disappear, steer them where no one is looking. Funny thing about stories: the first version, the real one, always gets swallowed by the second and third. All that is left out here are the edited copies, and in those copies the same anonymous hand keeps bending routes through a dead station that should not hear anything at all. I found the node that all his ghosts pass through. Now I just have to decide whether I am brave enough, or stupid enough, to follow.
zh:
我在中继站的一间维护壁龛里记录这些，因为这里的墙感觉更厚，像它们这回真会保守一个秘密。

过去六个小时我亲手一层层剥开贸易管理局的清单。以前坐这个岗位的经纪商以为自己很聪明，把图案藏在错误标签和"传输错误"里。他不够聪明。在那些重复项和幽灵货运里，埋着一簇永远不指向任何港口的交通标签，只是绕回天涯边缘上同一座已废弃的军用上行链路。联殖登记表说那座监听站多年前就沉寂了，可这些路由的时间戳都是新的。

酒吧故事里的每个人都在谈论一个能在飞船消失后找到它们、把它们引向没人看的地方的飞行员。故事有趣的地方在于：第一个版本，也就是真实的那个，总会被第二、第三个版本吞掉。在这外面剩下的只有被编辑过的副本，而在那些副本里，同一只匿名的手不断把航线绕过一座本不该听见任何东西的死站。我找到了他所有幽灵都会经过的那个节点。现在我只得决定，自己是够勇敢，还是够愚蠢，敢跟上去。

#en:
I should have left this place two jumps ago.

The ridge hums at night, like the rock is holding its breath with us. In the common room they pass around chipped mugs and the same stories, sanded down by a dozen retellings. No one ever starts with "I was there." It is always a cousin, a crew mate, a stranger at some port whose name they forgot. An engineer who comes when the air goes thin, touches a console, and the gauges swing back to green. People stop coughing. Filters stop screaming. Everyone is so grateful they do not ask what she changed.

The missioner let me see the notes, reluctant, like they were sacred. Dates, ship IDs, settlement codes. I recognized two routes from my own hauling days and felt stupid for not noticing the pattern sooner. Same failures, same "miracle," same consultant moving just ahead of the real breakdowns. This has been going on longer than anyone here wants to admit; you can see it in the way they flinch from their own records. I keep thinking about all the times I docked, saw flickering status boards, and assumed it was just frontier life. We all overlooked it, because the air kept flowing and nobody wants to stare too hard at the thing that keeps them breathing.
zh:
我两个跃迁之前就该离开这地方了。

山脊在夜里嗡鸣，像这块岩石在跟我们一道屏住呼吸。在公共室里，人们传来传去的是豁了口的杯子和同样的故事，被十来次转述磨得光滑。从没人以"我当时在场"开头。永远是某个表亲、某个同船的人、某个在港口遇到却忘了名字的陌生人。一名工程师，在空气变稀薄时到来，碰一下控制台，仪表就摆回绿色。人们不再咳嗽。过滤器不再尖叫。人人都感激得不去问她究竟改了什么。

那位传教士让我看了那些笔记，很不情愿，像那是圣物。日期、船号、定居点代码。我认出其中两条来自我自己跑运输的日子，为自己没更早注意到这个图案而觉得自己很蠢。同样的故障，同样的"奇迹"，同样的顾问总是刚好赶在真正的崩溃之前。这事持续得比这里任何人愿意承认的都久；你能从他们对自家记录的那种畏缩里看出来。我总想起我每一次停靠时，看到闪烁的状态板，都以为那只是边疆生活的常态。我们都忽略了它，因为空气还在流动，而没人愿意太用力地盯着那个让自己保持呼吸的东西。

#en: I am logging this off the main board, tucked under a maintenance stub no one bothers to audit. The relay I just walked through was gutted in a hurry, like somebody got spooked mid-job. Panels hanging, fuse trays half-ripped, error lights frozen mid-blink. That is not how you mothball hardware, that is how you run when orders change faster than your hands can keep up. Whatever this place was listening to, it soaked it up deep; you can feel it in the way comms go thin and tinny as soon as you slide into this sector, like the channel is already half-occupied by echoes from somewhere else.\n\nBack at the bar, no one talks about this straight. It is always a mutter over a drink, a sideways glance at the door. Pilots say traffic control has been "off" along the old war corridors, that ships slip a little too close to debris and no one files complaints because no one wants the attention. You start asking for specifics and voices drop, sentences trail off. I keep hearing the same thing in different words though: misjumps, unlogged wrecks, distress calls that never hit the right receivers. People act like if they describe it too clearly, whoever is listening out there will turn their head and notice them next.
zh: 我绕开主板上报这条记录，把它塞进一个没人费心审计的维护存根底下。我刚走过的那座中继站被匆忙掏空了，像有人在干活干到一半被吓到了。面板悬着，保险丝托盘被扯掉一半，错误灯冻在闪烁的半途。那不是封存硬件的方式，那是当命令变化快过你手速时逃命的方式。不管这地方当时在听什么，它都深深地吸了进去；你一滑进这个星区，通讯就变得又薄又尖，像那条频道已经被别处的回响占去了一半，这一点你能感觉得到。\n\n回到酒吧，没人把这事讲得直白。永远是一杯酒上一声嘟囔，朝门口斜一眼。飞行员说旧战争走廊沿线的交通管制一直"不对劲"，飞船滑得离碎片稍微太近，却没人投诉，因为没人想要那份关注。你一开始追问细节，声音就低下去，句子就断在半截。可我不断听到不同措辞说出的同一件事：错误跃迁、未入账的残骸、从未打到正确接收方的求救呼叫。人们表现得像只要把它描述得太清楚，外面那个正在听的人就会转过头来，下一个注意到他们。

#en: Primeway Flight is a small, semi-legitimate hauler outfit that works the under-served lanes around the derelict GC-8466 Depositron, taking contracts that larger lines deem unprofitable or too close to the insurance red zones. Port records describe them as "reliable, if chronically late," a reputation often blamed on their habit of lingering near drifting hulls and old traffic beacons to listen for distress calls and salvage rumors. Traders in the region note that Primeway crews swap corridor gossip as eagerly as they trade cargo manifests, repeating half-remembered tales about a vault ship that went dark and about quiet deals between GalBank clerks and UC officers who do not want their names in the same log. One dockside statement archived at a nearby station mentions the crew bickering loudly over a pilot's slurped noodles and mismatched socks while arguing whether the story of vented testbeds and redacted annexes is corporate myth or something far uglier. Whatever their internal frictions, Primeway Flight continues to chart courses uncomfortably close to GC-8466, citing "good salvage odds" while pretending not to notice how many transponders in that corridor have started flickering or falling silent.
zh: 主航飞行是一支规模不大、半合法化的货运船队，在弃船 GC-8466 沉积石号周边那些服务不足的航道上营生，接一些大型航线认为无利可图、或太靠近保险红区的合同。港口记录形容他们"可靠，只是慢性子"，这份名声常被归咎于他们习惯在漂流的船壳和旧交通信标附近逗留，偷听求救呼叫和打捞传言。该区域的商人指出，主航的船员交换走廊闲话的热情不亚于交换货运清单，反复讲述着半记半忘的故事——关于一艘陷入沉寂的金库船，关于银河银行文员与不愿名字出现在同一份日志里的联殖军官之间的安静交易。一份存于附近空间站的码头口述记录提到，船员们曾为一个飞行员吸溜面条和穿错的袜子的声音大声拌嘴，同时争论那个关于被抽空的试验台和被涂黑附件的故事，究竟是企业的神话，还是更丑陋的什么东西。不管他们内部有什么摩擦，主航飞行仍继续把航线画得离 GC-8466 近得令人不安，嘴上说着"打捞机会好"，同时假装没注意到那条走廊里有多少应答器开始闪烁或归于沉寂。

#en: I thought I was done being scared of numbers. Routes in, routes out, stress curves, tolerances it is all just math until the hull groans. But sitting here in the dark of this Vanguard hulk, listening to the residual power whisper through ruined conduits, I finally heard what the others meant when they said the lanes themselves sound wrong. The drive logs I pulled are not patrol profiles, they are something else sharp, stacked, like someone kept threading the same needle through narrower fabric, waiting for it to tear. The analysts back at that quiet little module told me, off the record, that certain vectors keep reappearing on ships that never should have shared charts. Now, sifting through this ship's black box, I see the same patterns buried under rewritten timestamps. People out in the fringe talk about a pilot who can slip a freighter through a sensor net like smoke, or drag a warship off its leash with a single corrected jump. It started as one lost convoy and a half-whispered complaint in a bar, but now the story has grown legs hulls going missing near dead listening posts, nav cores scrubbed clean except for that same curled signature. Whatever is tying all this together, it is not rumor anymore.
zh: 我以为自己已经不再怕数字了。航线进、航线出，应力曲线，容差——在船壳呻吟之前，一切都只是算术。可此刻坐在这艘先锋队船壳的黑暗里，听着残余电力在毁坏的导管里低语，我终于听懂了别人说"航道本身听起来不对劲"是什么意思。我调出的驱动日志不是巡逻剖面，而是别的东西——锋利、层层叠叠，像有人一遍遍把同一根针穿进更窄的布料，等着它撕裂。那座安静小模块上的分析师私下告诉我，某些矢量会不断出现在本不该共享星图的飞船上。如今，翻检这艘船的黑匣子，我看见同样的图案埋在重写过的时间戳底下。外缘的人谈论一个能把货船像烟一样送过传感器网、或用一个修正过的跃迁把战舰拽离牵引的飞行员。它起初只是一支失踪的运输队和酒吧里一声半低语的抱怨，可如今这故事长出了腿——飞船在死掉的监听站附近失踪，导航核心被擦得干干净净，只剩下同一个卷曲的特征。不管把这些串起来的是什么，它都不再只是传言了。

#en:
I am writing this between shifts, wedged behind a stack of mislabeled crates where the cams do not quite reach. The ship hums around me, same as it has for years, but it feels different now that I know how long we have been looking the other way.  

We got another batch of "scrap" yesterday, routed from a yard that is supposed to be half-dead. Seals blacked out, destination tags that loop through the same offworld pit before they vanish from the system. Nobody blinked. The loaders cursed about the weight, the clerk stamped the forms, and it slid into our hold like a hundred others.  

I should have noticed sooner. The route codes repeat, always back through that old mine that Deimos supposedly walked away from. I remember hearing about it over TerraBrew once, something about "reclamation" and "special contracts," but I filed it under spacer gossip and let it drift.  

Now the manifests keep glitching around those shipments, and I swear the automated checks skip entire lines when that mine comes up. Maybe it is nothing. Maybe it is everything.  

All I know is, somewhere out there is a hole in the rock swallowing hardware and names both, and we have been feeding it without even asking what it is for.
zh:
我在班次之间写下这些，挤在一堆贴错标签、摄像头照不太到的货箱后面。飞船在我四周嗡鸣，跟这些年一样，可如今它感觉不同了——因为我知道我们别过头去已经多久了。

昨天我们又收到一批"废料"，从一座据说半死的船坞发来。封条被涂黑，目的地标签在从系统里消失之前都会绕经同一个星球外的坑洞。没人眨眼。装卸工为重量咒骂，文员盖章，它就那样像上百件别的东西一样滑进了我们的货舱。

我本该更早注意到的。那些航路代码重复着，总是绕回那座据称火卫二弃之而去的旧矿场。我记得曾就着地球酿酒听人提起过它，什么"复垦"和"特殊合同"，可我把它归进太空人的闲话，任它飘走了。

如今那些货运周围的清单不断出错，我发誓当那座矿场出现时，自动检查会跳过整整几行。也许没什么。也许这就是一切。

我只知道，在外面的某处，岩石里有个洞，把硬件和名字一起吞下去；而我们一直在往里喂东西，甚至不问它是做什么用的。

#en:
I thought this would be routine, signing those papers at the GalBank kiosk, nodding along while they talked about risk coverage and "weather volatility." Just one more form so we could keep the farm. That was, what, early 2329? The clerk barely looked up from their slate. I barely read the fine print.

Now I am floating through this dead protection ship, and every time a body turns in the stale air, I see my own hands on that screen again, ticking boxes I did not understand. The files I pulled mention our parcel by grid, same as the Waggoner place, tucked into a list of "exposure flags" next to clinical notes about yield spikes and respiratory cases. Someone in an office somewhere tagged us as a line item and forgot to untick the box.

Back home the soil started misbehaving. First it was just more grain than we could store, then the dust that burned your throat if you worked past noon. We called inspectors, they shrugged it off, said weather again. Later in Gagarin, I heard dock rats mutter about shipments like ours and a woman who kept showing up wherever the numbers went strange. They joked that if your crops were too good to be true, you would see her shadow in the manifests before you saw her in your fields.
zh:
我以为这会是例行公事——在银河银行的柜员机前签那些文件，一边点头一边听他们谈风险覆盖和"天气波动"。不过是再多一份表格，好让我们保住农场。那是……2329 年初吧？那文员几乎没从数据板上抬头。我也几乎没读那些细则。

如今我漂在这艘死去的保护船里，每当一具尸体在陈腐的空气中翻转，我又看见自己的手按在那块屏幕上，勾着我看不懂的框。我调出的文件按网格提到了我们的地块，和瓦格纳家一样，被塞进一份"风险暴露标记"清单里，旁边是关于产量激增和呼吸道病例的临床笔记。某个办公室里的某个人把我们也标成了一条账目，然后忘了把那个框取消掉。

回家后，土壤开始不听话了。起初只是谷物多到我们存不下，然后是过了中午还在地里干活就会烧嗓子的灰尘。我们叫来检查员，他们耸耸肩，又说是天气。后来在加加林，我听码头老鼠们嘟囔着像我们这样的货运，以及一个女人——哪里数字变得古怪，她就出现在哪里。他们开玩笑说，要是你的庄稼好得不真实，你会先在清单上看到她的影子，然后才在自家田里见到她。

#en:
Started this file three months ago, when it was still just a nagging feeling in the back of my skull and a handful of "unrelated" accidents on my desk.  
I told myself I was chasing noise in the telemetry. Now the coincidences are stacked too neatly to ignore.

Every time a freighter tore itself open near that debris field, I saw the same microscopic bias in the plotted jump. Different captains, different hulls, same invisible hand on the numbers. Then came the backcountry wreck with a registry that should have been retired, orbiting right where the math said it would fail, and that nameless slate we pulled off a scavenger, full of "efficiency tweaks" that all bent in one direction.

Tonight, out here on this forgotten rock, the pattern closed in on a name. Buried in a bundle of reroute authorizations, maintenance notes, and one unsent request for an internal review, the same analyst's signature keeps surfacing, always just upstream of the disaster. I cross-checked routing timestamps with those misjumps and the quiet redirects through that comm hub they call a relay; every path backtracks to him. Whatever this Tariq really is, I have him narrowed to a handful of corridors and one last waypoint the others somehow missed.
zh:
三个月前开的这份档案，那时它还只是我后脑勺里一阵烦人的感觉，和我桌上几起"互不相关"的事故。

我告诉自己，我追的只是遥测里的噪声。可如今那些巧合堆得太整齐，无法忽视。

每次有货船在那片碎片场附近裂开，我都在标绘出的跃迁里看到同样那点微观的偏差。不同的船长、不同的船壳，同一只看不见的手按在数字上。然后是那具乡野残骸，登记号本该早已退役，轨道恰好停在其算式所说会失效的位置；还有我们从一名拾荒者身上取下的那块无名数据板，满是全都朝同一个方向弯的"效率调整"。

今晚，在这块被遗忘的岩石上，那图案收紧到了一个名字上。埋在一捆改道授权、维护笔记和一份未发出的内部复核申请里，同一个分析师的签名不断浮出，总是刚好在灾难的上游。我把路由时间戳与那些错误跃迁、以及经由他们称作中继站的通讯枢纽进行的安静重定向交叉核对；每一条路径都回溯到他身上。不管这个塔里克究竟是什么，我已经把他缩小到几条走廊和一个别人不知怎的漏掉的最后航点。
